attacks.claim: The nightly single-statement job on the primary cannot finish in its window at the plan's own sizing. 30% of 2.1M MAU is about 630k users, which is 52x the 12k staging run. Linear extrapolation gives about 36 hours (41 min × 52.5), and a join over 340k recipes will likely scale worse than linear. The run overlaps the next night's job and holds heavy load on the only write primary. (The first pass's 'about 4 years' figure is an arithmetic error, but the conclusion holds.)
attacks.evidence: "Staging run: 12,000 synthetic pantry users completed in 41 minutes." / "30% of MAU create a pantry within 90 days." / "on the primary"

attacks.claim: One long statement on the shared primary has no stated batching, timeout, checkpointing, retry, or idempotency. A failure loses all progress. Long-running load threatens latency for the whole API, and no alerting or overrun handling is described.
attacks.evidence: "score every recipe in the catalog (340k recipes) in a single SQL statement joining pantry_items x recipe_ingredients on the primary, then upsert the top 50"

attacks.claim: The staging result is the only compute evidence, and it is unqualified. Synthetic pantry size, recipe count, and primary versus replica are not stated, and it was run at 1/50 of target scale. Nothing shows that it predicts production.
attacks.evidence: "12,000 synthetic pantry users completed in 41 minutes."

attacks.claim: At the sizing assumption the job writes about 31.5M upserts a night (630k × 50) and does heavy join reads on the primary. No IOPS, compute, or storage budget is given, and nothing says whether the primary or replicas need to be upsized. Nor does the plan consider incremental recompute only for users whose pantry changed.
attacks.evidence: "top 50 per user." / "for each user with a pantry, score every recipe"

attacks.claim: The plan's top churn reason is setup and typing burden (38%). The 15-item gate with required expiry dates adds exactly that burden, and all value is withheld until it is cleared. Most users will likely abandon before unlock, so the feature may worsen the larger problem while addressing the 22% one.
attacks.evidence: "unlocks once a user has entered at least 15 items with expiry dates" / "Too much setup / typing to get useful suggestions — 38%"

attacks.claim: The success target is inconsistent with the sizing assumption. 25% of MAU unlocking in 60 days implies that about 83% of the users who create a pantry (30% in 90 days) reach 15 dated items, even faster. This is implausible given the friction and has no supporting data. The 15-item threshold itself is justified only as 'match quality' with no evidence.
attacks.evidence: "25% of MAU unlock Pantry Match within 60 days." / "30% of MAU create a pantry within 90 days."

attacks.claim: The matching spec is underspecified. The expiry weighting formula is undefined, quantity and unit handling is not addressed (a score that ignores quantity makes 'I made this' updates pointless), and staples are hardcoded to four items. Items without an expiry date have no defined scoring.
attacks.evidence: "weighted by expiry proximity, with pantry staples (salt, oil, water, pepper) always counted as present."

attacks.claim: Pantry contents, expiry dates, and post-cooking quantity updates form a per-user behavioral dataset. No retention, deletion, or analytics-scope statement is given.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention/deletion policy for pantry_items and quantity updates.

attacks.claim: No feature flag, kill switch, or rollback is described for the rollout or for the nightly job overwriting pantry_matches.
The timeline has no slack, and no load test at production volume is planned before the week-6 beta, even though the job is the main risk.
There is no mention of screen reader labels for the progress bar or carousel, or of keyboard access for the autocomplete.
Validation and bounds for quantity, unit, and expiry inputs are not specified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: input validation for the pantry form.
